assessment.nobel_worthiness: A clear underlying principle: a unified Lagrangian that propagates electronic structure and nuclei together, making ab initio molecular dynamics practical. It reshaped the simulation of liquids, interfaces, bond breaking and condensed-phase chemistry, and it sits exactly at the physics-chemistry border. Impact is broad and quantitative, and the derived methods are universal in the field.
assessment.attribution: The 1985 paper has exactly two authors and the credit is unambiguous, which gives a clean and easily explained citation. I would keep both.
assessment.maturity: Four decades of use, broad independent adoption and a stable interpretation; recognition is overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees it as method development of sufficient chemical weight after earlier computational chemistry prizes.
Parrinello also appears under other computational candidates, so the citation should be anchored to this discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Massively parallel sequencing-by-synthesis changed the scale of genome reading by orders of magnitude and underpins modern genomics and medicine. The core is chemistry: reversible terminators, fluorescent nucleotides and clustered amplification on surfaces. Generative potential is very large.
assessment.attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman originated the Solexa sequencing-by-synthesis concept and chemistry; other credited names (Rothberg, Ju, Mayer) have claims for related platforms. A two-person citation focused on the Solexa chemistry is defensible but contested by platform history.
assessment.maturity: Mature: two decades of routine global use and many independent platforms. Timing is ripe.
uncertainties: The split of credit among competing platforms (pyrosequencing, Solexa, Illumina, others) and the role of commercial development is unresolved.
Whether the committee regards it as chemistry rather than biology or medicine; Sanger sequencing was recognised in 1980.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Biomolecular condensates formed by liquid-liquid phase separation offer a physical-chemical principle for organizing cells without membranes. It brings polymer physics and thermodynamics to cell biology and opens new questions in disease and drug discovery. I find the conceptual originality high, though the quantitative framework is still maturing.
assessment.attribution: Brangwynne and Hyman showed P granules behave as liquids; Rosen showed multivalent interactions drive phase separation in vitro. Pappu and Mittag contributed physical and sequence-grammar understanding. A three-person prize is plausible but others have a strong claim.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly growing but still debated: functional significance in vivo, artefacts of overexpression and which condensates are truly phase-separated remain disputed. Possibly slightly early.
uncertainties: Whether physiological relevance is established well enough.
Whether the discovery is chemistry rather than cell biology.
Claims by Pappu, Mittag and others complicate the three-person limit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Hijacking the ubiquitin-proteasome system with bifunctional PROTACs and molecular glues converts binding into degradation, enabling targeting of proteins previously considered undruggable. The mechanism is clear and the capability is genuinely new, with clinical candidates in trials.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies conceived and demonstrated PROTACs; Handa and Ito identified cereblon as the thalidomide target underlying molecular glue degraders. Ciulli, Gray and Sakamoto also contributed important steps. The allocation is difficult.
assessment.maturity: Strong preclinical and growing clinical evidence, though no fully approved PROTAC drug yet; recognition may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Competing claims for first-in-class demonstrations, and a compound discovery whose PROTAC and glue parts may need different recognition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pd-catalysed C-N cross-coupling is a general, mechanistically well understood tool for making aryl amines, ubiquitous in pharmaceuticals and materials. Its impact is enormous and the concept is clear and explainable to a broad audience.
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig independently developed the general catalytic ligand-controlled methodology; Kosugi's earlier tin-amide work is a precursor. A two-person prize is the natural configuration, and Migita/Kosugi-style antecedents complicate it only slightly.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature, with decades of independent confirmation and industrial use. Palladium cross-coupling was recognised in 2010, which may make the committee see it as an extension.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views it as an incremental follow-up to the 2010 cross-coupling prize.
Role of Kosugi and other precursors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Descriptor-based theory (d-band model, scaling relations, volcano plots) turned catalyst design into a quantitative, predictive science. As a physicist I value the clear principle linking electronic structure to reactivity, with experimental validation and real discovery of new catalysts.
assessment.attribution: Nørskov is the central originator; Mavrikakis, Scheffler and Rossmeisl contributed in distinct ways. A single-laureate or two-laureate configuration is conceivable, and the d-band model involved Bjørk Hammer, who is not in the credited names.
assessment.maturity: Mature and widely adopted, with experimental confirmation across many reactions; some limits of scaling relations are now being explored.
uncertainties: Credit beyond the supplied names (the d-band model co-originator is not credited here).
How much practical catalyst discovery follows directly from descriptors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Single-molecule electrical readout through nanopores connects physical principles of ion transport with chemistry and sequencing. It delivered long-read, portable sequencing and a general platform for single-molecule sensing. Clear physical principle and a genuinely new capability.
assessment.attribution: Kasianowicz, Branton and Deamer demonstrated polynucleotide translocation in 1996; Bayley engineered protein pores; Akeson showed base discrimination. Credit is spread over several steps and authors, making a three-person selection hard.
assessment.maturity: Commercial products exist and are widely used; accuracy and applications continue to improve, though the field is still evolving.
uncertainties: Allocation among Kasianowicz, Branton, Deamer, Bayley and Akeson is unresolved.
Whether the prize should emphasize the sensing principle or the sequencing technology.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The dye-sensitized nanocrystalline solar cell introduced a new photoelectrochemical architecture with clear charge-separation physics, and it seeded a wide field of molecular and later perovskite photovoltaics. The principle is original and elegant.
assessment.attribution: The 1991 O'Regan and Grätzel paper is the decisive contribution, so a two-person prize is natural; Hagfeldt contributed later mechanistic and efficiency work.
assessment.maturity: Mature: three decades of confirmation, though commercial impact has been more modest than expected, and efficiency progress passed to perovskites. Timeliness is a question.
uncertainties: Limited commercial impact compared with the discovery's scientific influence.
Whether the committee prefers the successor technology (perovskites) instead.
